newsitem.title: USA: AMR says "time to make deal" with pilots.
newsitem.headline: AMR says "time to make deal" with pilots.

text.p: Robert Crandall, chairman of AMR Corp., parent of American Airlines, said Wednesday it was time to reach a labour agreement with the carrier's pilots and to end a long-time dispute over wages and the flying of new regional jets.
"It is time to make a deal," Crandall said.

Crandall made his comments as a special Presidential Emergency Board was winding up five days of hearings on the dispute before making recommendations to President Clinton and the two parties on resolving their differences.
He said the lengthy negotiations have been harmful both to the company and employees and he hoped the special board would make recommendations that were acceptable to both the company and the union.
But Crandall gave no hint that there was any change in the company's position on pay increases being sought by the pilots' union, the Allied Pilots Association.
Nor did he say if American would change its position on refusing to allow higher-paid APA pilots to fly the new regional jets American plans to buy for its commuter airline.
American wants the commuter planes to be flown by lower-paid pilots so American's commuter line, American Eagle, can be competitive with the low-cost commuter lines operated by other major carriers.

Under federal law, the emergency board must submit its recommendations for settlement to the president and the two parties by March 17. If the parties do not agree to the terms of the settlement, the union is free to strike.
AMR's stock was up $2.875 at $83.125 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
